docs.mac.features.meta.title: Features - macOS - TypeWhisper
docs.mac.features.meta.description: A comprehensive overview of TypeWhisper's capabilities on macOS.
docs.mac.features.title: Features
docs.mac.features.subtitle: A comprehensive overview of TypeWhisper's capabilities on macOS.
docs.mac.features.dictation.title: System-Wide Dictation
docs.mac.features.dictation.desc: Use a global hotkey to start and stop recording from any app. Choose between push-to-talk (hold to record), toggle mode (press to start/stop), or modifier-key hotkeys. Transcribed text is automatically pasted into the active text field.
docs.mac.features.streaming.title: Streaming Preview
docs.mac.features.streaming.desc: WhisperKit and Apple SpeechAnalyzer provide live partial results while you speak. With Parakeet and engines without native streaming, the overlay falls back to showing available text and current progress as soon as results arrive.
docs.mac.features.ai.title: AI Workflows
docs.mac.features.ai.desc1: Process transcribed text through workflows before it gets pasted. TypeWhisper includes templates for translation, formatting, summarization, and app-specific cleanup.
docs.mac.features.ai.desc2: Connect Apple Intelligence (on-device), Groq, OpenAI, Gemini, or another LLM integration, then arrange providers and optional models in one global fallback list. Workflows inherit that order by default; selecting an explicit workflow provider keeps that workflow on one strict provider call.
docs.mac.features.ai.learn: Learn how workflows work, how prompt instructions are applied, and what to check if nothing changes.
docs.mac.features.ai.imgAlt: Workflows settings with the global LLM fallback and three active workflows
docs.mac.features.dictionary.title: Dictionary
docs.mac.features.dictionary.desc: Teach TypeWhisper domain-specific vocabulary. Add custom terms, define corrections for commonly misrecognized words, and turn on Premium > Learn from Corrections to build your personal dictionary over time. Import community term packs and use licensed industry packs for fields such as real estate, architecture, and legal drafting.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.desc2: The dictionary has two parts: custom terms can be passed into transcription when the engine supports them, and dictionary corrections are applied automatically after transcription. You do not need to manually force the dictionary to run.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.desc3: With Parakeet, custom terms can stay fully local. Enable vocabulary boosting and Parakeet will use those terms on-device during transcription, while post-transcription corrections still run automatically.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.boostingDes: Boosting controls how closely Parakeet's initial result must resemble a Dictionary Term before local vocabulary rescoring may use it. Lower thresholds are more aggressive and may catch wider variations; higher thresholds are more cautious and reduce false matches.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.boostingAut: Recommended starting point. Parakeet chooses a threshold automatically based on the number of active terms.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.boostingStr: The most aggressive preset. Use it when a distinctive name is still missed often. It increases recall, but can produce more false matches.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.boostingBal: A more cautious middle setting. Try it if Strong replaces similar ordinary words.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.boostingPre: Requires a close match. Use it when the term resembles an ordinary word and avoiding false matches matters more than catching every variation.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.boostingAdv: Sets the threshold manually. Lower values are more aggressive; higher values are more cautious. Adjust it in small steps and repeat the same test sentence.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.boostingExa: Example: For a name such as Kazumi, start with Auto. If Parakeet still misses it, try Strong. If Strong starts inserting Kazumi for similar ordinary words, move to Balanced or Precise.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.boostingNot: These thresholds affect Parakeet only and require Enable Vocabulary Boosting in the Parakeet integration. Other engines may use Terms as hints but ignore the thresholds. Boosting does not train the base model and is separate from Dictionary Corrections, which still run after transcription.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.autoLearnDe: Learn from Corrections runs after TypeWhisper inserts dictated text into the target app; there is no separate per-workflow switch. TypeWhisper briefly watches the inserted text through macOS Accessibility. If you manually correct exactly one word and the diff is high-confidence, it saves a Dictionary Correction. Sentence rewrites, deletions, and ambiguous edits are skipped on purpose so TypeWhisper does not learn bad replacements.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.autoLearnFe: When a correction is learned, TypeWhisper shows feedback such as Saved to Dictionary: “wrong” -> “right” with an Undo action. Learned entries can be reviewed in Dictionary > Auto-learned / Corrections. If no feedback appears, either nothing safe was learned or the target app did not expose the edited text reliably enough.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.autoLearnTe: Turn on Learn from Corrections under Settings > Premium, dictate a short sentence into a normal text field, manually fix one misrecognized word, then press Return or Tab, send the message, or leave the field. Look for the learned-correction feedback and the Auto-learned dictionary entry.
docs.mac.features.dictionary.imgAlt: Dictionary with custom terms and corrections
docs.mac.features.snippets.title: Snippets
docs.mac.features.snippets.descBefore: Define trigger phrases that expand into longer text blocks. Snippets support dynamic placeholders like
docs.mac.features.snippets.descAfter: for automatic date, time, and clipboard insertion.
docs.mac.features.snippets.imgAlt: Snippets with trigger phrases and placeholders
docs.mac.features.fileTranscription.desc: Drag and drop audio or video files to transcribe them in batch. Supports all common formats (MP3, WAV, M4A, MP4, MOV, and more). Export results as SRT or WebVTT subtitles with accurate timestamps.
docs.mac.features.whisperMode.title: Whisper Mode
docs.mac.features.whisperMode.desc: Boost microphone gain for quiet speech or noisy environments. Turn on Whisper Mode (AGC) for all dictations under Settings > Advanced, or set it for a single workflow.
docs.mac.features.translation.title: Translation
docs.mac.features.translation.desc: Apple Translate provides on-device translation between many language pairs. In Workflows, the Translation template can use Apple Translate on macOS 15+ or LLM Prompt mode for provider-based translation. WhisperKit can also translate speech from any supported language to English.
docs.mac.features.history.title: Transcription History
docs.mac.features.history.desc1: All transcriptions are saved locally with their time, the app they were dictated into, and the engine and model used. Edit an entry in place and switch between Final, Original, and Changes to see what was corrected.
docs.mac.features.history.desc2: History opens in its own window. The sidebar holds Inbox, All History, With Audio, and Failed, and groups entries by device. Search the text, filter by date or app, and sort the list. Select several entries to copy them, export them as Markdown, plain text, or JSON, mark them complete, or delete them. Open the window with Open History under Settings > History & Sync.
docs.mac.features.history.imgAlt: History window with the list of transcriptions and the selected entry
docs.mac.features.home.title: Home Dashboard
docs.mac.features.home.desc: Home opens with your dashboard. Your Activity shows four numbers: words, average words per minute, apps used, and time saved. Recent Transcriptions lists your latest dictations. From there you reach the full statistics and the complete history.
docs.mac.features.home.imgAlt: Home dashboard with activity numbers and recent transcriptions
docs.mac.features.statistics.title: Statistics
docs.mac.features.statistics.desc1: Statistics shows how you dictate over a week, a month, or all time. Eight numbers summarize the period: days active, current and longest streak, transcriptions, words, average words per minute, apps used, and time saved. Below them you find the activity per day, your top apps, the models used, and the usage by time of day.
docs.mac.features.statistics.desc2: TypeWhisper keeps these figures on your Mac as daily totals: counts, words, duration, apps, models, and hours. They contain no dictated text and stay complete when the history is shortened or switched off.
docs.mac.features.statistics.imgAlt: Statistics with eight figures, the activity per day, top apps, and the models used
docs.mac.features.plugins.title: Integrations
docs.mac.features.plugins.desc: Extend TypeWhisper under Settings > Integrations. My Plugins lists what is installed, with settings, updates, and downloaded local models. Discover shows the available plugins with search, a filter by function, sorting by popularity or name, and a switch for community plugins. Install Plugin adds a plugin from a file.
docs.mac.features.plugins.imgAlt: Integrations settings with Apple Speech as the installed plug-in
docs.mac.fileTranscription.meta.title: File Transcription - macOS - TypeWhisper
docs.mac.fileTranscription.meta.descript: Transcribe audio and video files manually or automatically from a watched folder on macOS.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.title: File Transcription
docs.mac.fileTranscription.subtitle: Transcribe audio and video files manually, or automate incoming files with Watch Folder.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.imgAlt: File Transcription settings with drop area, folder selection, engine, output format, and the switch for deleting source files
docs.mac.fileTranscription.manual.title: Manual File Transcription
docs.mac.fileTranscription.manual.desc1: Use File Transcription when you want to transcribe existing audio or video files without recording a new dictation. Drag files into the drop area or choose them from the file picker. In Finder, select audio or video files and choose the action Transcribe with TypeWhisper: TypeWhisper adds them to the list and opens File Transcription.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.manual.desc2: Manual batches process only the files you add yourself. Once files are in the list, choose the engine and the language before you start. A model picker appears when the engine offers more than one model, and a task picker when the engine can translate.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.watchFolder.d: Watch Folder monitors a folder you choose in TypeWhisper settings. When a supported audio or video file appears there, TypeWhisper queues it and transcribes it automatically.
Watch Folder keeps listening for new files until you stop watching. This is useful for recorder exports, downloads, or other folders where new media files arrive repeatedly.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.output.title: Output Files
docs.mac.fileTranscription.output.desc1: TypeWhisper writes the transcript artifact first. Choose Markdown, plain text, SRT, or WebVTT as the output format.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.output.desc2: For Watch Folder, transcripts are written to the selected output folder. If no output folder is configured, transcripts are written next to the source file in the watched folder.
When this Watch Folder option is enabled, TypeWhisper deletes the original source audio or video file after the job finishes successfully and the transcript output has been written.
The source file is removed directly by the app. It is not deliberately moved to the macOS Trash.
If transcription fails, TypeWhisper keeps the source file in place so you can retry or inspect the problem.
Only enable this option when you no longer need the original files or you already keep another backup.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.setup.title: Basic Setup
docs.mac.fileTranscription.setup.step2: For manual batches, drop files into the file area or choose them from the file picker.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.setup.step3: For Watch Folder, choose the watched folder and, optionally, a separate output folder.
docs.mac.fileTranscription.setup.step4: Choose the engine, language behavior, output format, and whether source files should be deleted after successful Watch Folder transcription.
docs.mac.installation.meta.title: Installation - macOS - TypeWhisper
docs.mac.installation.title: Installation
docs.mac.installation.subtitle: Install the stable macOS {macSeries} release.
docs.mac.installation.release.title: macOS {macSeries}
docs.mac.installation.release.desc: TypeWhisper 1.7 adds iCloud synchronization for History and Inbox, a redesigned History window, file transcription from Finder, spoken submit and Inline Commands for workflows, configurable cancellation, and expanded plugin capabilities.
docs.mac.installation.highlights.title: What's new in 1.7
docs.mac.installation.highlights.item1: iCloud synchronization for History and Inbox, and a redesigned History window with device grouping, filtering, and search.
docs.mac.installation.highlights.item2: File transcription from Finder, and web media through the optional Web Link plugin.
docs.mac.installation.highlights.item3: Spoken submit and Inline Commands for workflows, and a choice of how Escape cancels a dictation: double, single, or immediate.
docs.mac.installation.highlights.item4: Plugin pages, optional providers that use authenticated command-line tools, and the Vercel AI Gateway as an optional plugin for transcription and LLM processing.
docs.mac.installation.highlights.item5: Improvements to recording startup, model restoration, text insertion, cancellation, and transcription recovery. Dictation Recovery keeps the last three successful dictations for up to 24 hours, so you can retry an incomplete result.
docs.mac.installation.highlights.item6: Number formatting with a threshold under Settings > Dictation > Output Formatting: Always, 10 and above, or 100 and above.
docs.mac.installation.upgrade.title: Before upgrading
docs.mac.installation.upgrade.desc: When upgrading from 1.6, export your settings under Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore before replacing the app. After the first launch, confirm Microphone and Accessibility permissions and run a short test dictation before returning to your normal workflow. Plugin releases built for 1.7 require TypeWhisper 1.7.0 or later.
docs.mac.installation.sync.title: iCloud sync in 1.7
docs.mac.installation.sync.desc: Automatic iCloud Sync is available in 1.7. Premium sync offers two modes: Automatic iCloud Sync through TypeWhisper's private iCloud container, or Cloud Folder with iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Syncthing, or a custom folder. Both modes sync your dictionary and snippets. Sync History & Inbox is a separate switch that you turn on for each Mac under Settings > History & Sync. Audio is synced for new entries only, and only when you enable it.
docs.mac.installation.requirements.title: System Requirements
docs.mac.installation.requirements.intel: Apple Intelligence and SpeechAnalyzer require macOS 26+
docs.mac.installation.download.title: Download
docs.mac.installation.download.descBefor: Download the latest stable DMG from
docs.mac.installation.download.channels: Release candidates and daily builds stay on preview channels and do not flow through Homebrew. For most users, the latest stable release is the right choice.
docs.mac.installation.homebrew.title: Homebrew
docs.mac.installation.firstLaunch.title: First Launch
docs.mac.installation.firstLaunch.desc: TypeWhisper appears as an icon in the menu bar. Open Settings to download your first model, configure your hotkey, and grant Microphone plus Accessibility access. Once that is done, you can complete your first dictation immediately.
docs.mac.rules.meta.title: Workflows - macOS - TypeWhisper
docs.mac.rules.meta.description: Configure website, app, hotkey, manual, and fallback workflows for dictation, selected-text processing, translation, prompts, and behavior in TypeWhisper.
docs.mac.rules.title: Workflows
docs.mac.rules.subtitle: Create website, app, hotkey, manual, and fallback workflows for dictation and direct text processing.
docs.mac.rules.howWork.title: How Workflows Work
docs.mac.rules.howWork.desc: When you start dictating, TypeWhisper matches the current browser URL first, then the active app, against your enabled workflows. Matching workflows can override language, task, engine, translation mode, prompts, and related behavior automatically. Hotkey workflows can also process the current selection or clipboard directly without recording audio. The active workflow name is shown as a badge in the indicator together with why it matched.
docs.mac.rules.palette.title: Quick Start with the Workflow Palette
docs.mac.rules.palette.desc: The Workflow Palette runs a workflow on text you have selected or copied, without a recording. It lists your workflows with the Manual trigger.
docs.mac.rules.palette.step1: Create a workflow with the Manual trigger under Settings > Workflows. For a first test, pick the Custom Workflow template and enter the instruction from the example below.
docs.mac.rules.palette.step2: Assign a Palette shortcut under Settings > Hotkeys > Workflow Palette.
docs.mac.rules.palette.step3: Select or copy text in any app and press the shortcut.
docs.mac.rules.palette.step4: Choose the workflow. TypeWhisper processes the text and inserts the result.
docs.mac.rules.palette.input: Tomorrow call Anna at 10, send revised pricing, and book a follow-up for Friday.
docs.mac.rules.palette.instruction: Turn the text into a short bullet list. Keep only the actionable points.
docs.mac.rules.palette.output:
- Call Anna at 10 tomorrow
- Send revised pricing
- Book a follow-up for Friday
docs.mac.rules.palette.helpLink: The FAQ lists what to check.
docs.mac.rules.matching.title: Trigger Types
docs.mac.rules.matching.siteOnly.title: Website
docs.mac.rules.matching.siteOnly.desc1: Website workflows work across browsers. Use one or more domains; a workflow for
docs.mac.rules.matching.appOnly.title: App
docs.mac.rules.matching.appOnly.desc: App workflows activate as soon as one of the selected apps is active. Use one or more apps for tools like Mail, Slack, Terminal, or browsers when a website condition is not needed.
docs.mac.rules.matching.hotkey.title: Hotkey
docs.mac.rules.matching.hotkey.desc: Hotkey workflows run when you press their assigned shortcut. They can start dictation or process selected text and do not compete with automatic app or website matching.
docs.mac.rules.matching.manual.title: Manual
docs.mac.rules.matching.manual.desc: Manual workflows are available from the Workflow Palette. They run only when you choose them directly.
docs.mac.rules.matching.fallback.title: Always fallback
docs.mac.rules.matching.fallback.desc: An Always workflow becomes the global fallback. It only applies when no more specific workflow matches.
docs.mac.rules.priority.title: Priority
docs.mac.rules.priority.desc: TypeWhisper resolves automatic workflow matches in this order:
docs.mac.rules.priority.manualHotkeyNote: Manual and hotkey workflows are direct actions. They run from the Workflow Palette or their assigned shortcut instead of being selected by app or URL matching.
docs.mac.rules.creating.title: Creating a Workflow
docs.mac.rules.creating.desc: Go to Settings > Workflows and click "New Workflow". Pick a template, choose one trigger type, then configure the fields for that trigger and the behavior you want:
docs.mac.rules.creating.apps.label: Apps
docs.mac.rules.creating.apps.desc: Limit the workflow to one or more selected apps
docs.mac.rules.creating.websites.label: Websites
docs.mac.rules.creating.websites.desc: Match browser tabs by one or more domains or subdomain patterns
docs.mac.rules.creating.language.label: Language
docs.mac.rules.creating.language.desc: Keep auto-detect, pin one language, or restrict recognition to likely languages
docs.mac.rules.creating.task.label: Task
docs.mac.rules.creating.task.desc: Transcribe or Translate where the selected engine supports it
For Translation workflows, choose Apple Translate on-device on macOS 15+ or LLM Prompt mode.
docs.mac.rules.creating.engine.label: Engine
docs.mac.rules.creating.engine.desc: WhisperKit, Parakeet TDT, Apple SpeechAnalyzer (macOS 26+), or any add-on engine
docs.mac.rules.creating.prompt.label: Prompt
docs.mac.rules.creating.prompt.desc: Workflow-specific LLM prompt instructions for automatic post-processing
docs.mac.rules.creating.promptProvider.d: Inherit the ordered global LLM fallback list, or select one provider for a strict single-provider call
docs.mac.rules.creating.manualShortcut.d: Assign one or more shortcuts to run this workflow on demand, either by starting dictation or by processing the current selection/clipboard directly
docs.mac.rules.creating.autoSubmit.label: Press Enter after inserting
docs.mac.rules.creating.autoSubmit.desc: Choose when TypeWhisper presses Enter after inserting the text: never, always, when you press Enter during dictation, or when the dictation ends with “press enter” or “press return”
docs.mac.rules.creating.inlineCommands.d: For Dictation Only workflows: detects a spoken instruction such as “write this as a friendly email”, removes it from the text, and applies it to the dictation
docs.mac.rules.creating.priority.label: Priority
docs.mac.rules.creating.priority.desc: Break ties between workflows in the same automatic match tier
docs.mac.rules.creating.imgAlt: Workflow list with three active workflows and their triggers
docs.mac.rules.manualShortcut.title: Hotkey Workflows
docs.mac.rules.manualShortcut.desc: You can assign one or more shortcuts to a workflow and choose what those shortcuts do. Start Dictation uses the normal recording path with that workflow's settings. Process Selected Text skips recording, reads the current accessibility selection, falls back to Cmd+C and then the clipboard when needed, and inserts the processed result through the same path as the Workflow Palette.
docs.mac.rules.languageEngineHotkeys.des: Create one Dictation Only workflow for each language and engine combination you want to trigger directly.
docs.mac.rules.languageEngineHotkeys.ste: Add a Dictation Only workflow for English, set Spoken Language to English, choose WhisperKit plus the model you want, and assign a Start Dictation hotkey.
Add a second Dictation Only workflow for Norwegian, set Spoken Language to Norwegian, choose the local Whisper engine plus its model, and assign a different Start Dictation hotkey.
Leave Transcription Engine on Use Global Engine when the workflow should follow the default engine under Settings > Dictation instead.
Use Process Selected Text hotkeys for selection-based cleanup or prompts; they do not record audio and therefore do not need a transcription engine or model.
docs.mac.rules.languageEngineHotkeys.not: This keeps the global engine unchanged while each dictation hotkey can still force its own language, engine, and model.
docs.mac.rules.promptOverride.title: Prompt Instructions
docs.mac.rules.promptOverride.intro: A prompt is the instruction of a workflow. The workflow sends the transcribed or selected text together with its instruction to the LLM provider and inserts the processed result.
docs.mac.rules.promptOverride.templates: Templates such as Cleaned Text, Email Reply, or Checklist bring their instruction with them. With the Custom Workflow template you write the instruction yourself in the Behavior step.
docs.mac.rules.promptOverride.desc: LLM Prompt workflows can attach prompt instructions to a specific context. Leave the provider on the global setting to inherit the ordered LLM fallback list, or select one provider when this workflow must make a strict single-provider call.
docs.mac.rules.globalLLMFallbacks.title: Global LLM fallback list
docs.mac.rules.globalLLMFallbacks.desc1: At the top of Settings > Workflows, add providers with an optional model and drag them into the order TypeWhisper should try. Inherited prompts and LLM workflows move to the next entry when a provider is unavailable, cannot restore, is rate-limited, hits a network or API error, or returns no text.
docs.mac.rules.globalLLMFallbacks.desc2: A workflow with an explicitly selected provider does not use the list. It makes one strict call to that provider. If every inherited fallback fails, TypeWhisper shows a combined error and does not insert replacement text.
docs.mac.rules.globalLLMFallbacks.desc3: This list is separate from the Always workflow trigger: Always chooses which workflow runs when no more specific workflow matches, while the LLM fallback list chooses the provider attempt order inside inherited prompt processing.
docs.mac.rules.multipleEngines.title: Multiple Engines
docs.mac.rules.multipleEngines.desc: Dictation Only workflows can override the transcription engine and model used for that hotkey. TypeWhisper can keep multiple engines loaded in memory during a session for instant switching. Set Auto-unload model to Never if you want previously loaded local models restored at launch; any active auto-unload policy keeps startup lazy and reloads the selected/downloaded model on first real use. Configure this in Settings > Advanced.
docs.mac.rules.formatting.title: App-aware Formatting
docs.mac.rules.formatting.desc1: App-aware formatting is a lightweight formatting pass, not a semantic or AI-based app detection feature. The global toggle under Settings > Dictation > Output Formatting only enables this pass. You only see a visible effect when the matched workflow also sets an Output Format.
docs.mac.rules.formatting.desc2: When dictation finishes, TypeWhisper passes the matched workflow's output format into the post-processing pipeline. If app-aware formatting is enabled, that formatting step runs before workflow text processing, snippets, and dictionary corrections.
docs.mac.rules.formatting.none.label: None
docs.mac.rules.formatting.none.desc: Disable additional formatting for this workflow.
docs.mac.rules.formatting.auto.label: Auto-Detect
docs.mac.rules.formatting.auto.desc: Choose a format from a fixed app bundle ID mapping. Known Markdown apps include Obsidian, Notion, Typora, Bear, and Ulysses. Known HTML apps include Apple Mail and Outlook. Known code apps include Xcode, VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Terminal, and iTerm. Unknown apps fall back to plain text.
docs.mac.rules.formatting.markdown.label: Markdown
docs.mac.rules.formatting.markdown.desc: Normalize list-like lines such as - item, * item, or dictated bullet item into Markdown list items.
docs.mac.rules.formatting.html.label: HTML

docs.mac.rules.faq.title: FAQ
docs.mac.rules.faq.q1.question: Why does TypeWhisper just type my prompt text?
docs.mac.rules.faq.q1.answer: Because instructions are configuration, not voice triggers. If you say the instruction out loud, TypeWhisper transcribes exactly what you said. Set the instruction in a workflow, then dictate the content you want transformed. If you want to speak the instruction, turn on Inline Commands in a Dictation Only workflow.
docs.mac.rules.faq.q2.question: Why does my workflow seem to do nothing?
docs.mac.rules.faq.q2.answer: Usually one of three things is missing: the workflow is not enabled, its trigger does not match the current app or website, or neither the inherited global LLM fallback list nor the workflow's explicit provider has a ready provider.
docs.mac.rules.faq.q3.question: Do templates and custom workflows work differently?
docs.mac.rules.faq.q3.answer: No. Both are applied after transcription and before insertion. Templates ship with their purpose built in, while a Custom Workflow depends on the instruction and provider you set.
docs.mac.rules.faq.q4.question: When should a workflow run automatically?
docs.mac.rules.faq.q4.answer: Use an app, website, hotkey, or Always trigger when one context should always get the same processing. That is useful for turning Mail dictation into polished emails or formatting meeting notes in a single tool.
docs.mac.rules.faq.q5.question: Can workflows trigger actions or plugins instead of plain text output?
docs.mac.rules.faq.q5.answer: Yes. A workflow can send its result to an action plugin as its Action Target instead of inserting text. That is how workflows like Linear issue creation or Obsidian note capture are wired up.
docs.mac.rules.faq.q6.question: Do I need placeholders in my instruction?
docs.mac.rules.faq.q6.answer: No. TypeWhisper passes the instruction and the text separately to the LLM provider. In practice, write the transformation you want, such as "Rewrite this as a polite email" or "Turn this into bullet points."
docs.mac.troubleshooting.meta.title: Troubleshooting - macOS - TypeWhisper
docs.mac.troubleshooting.meta.descriptio: Solutions for common TypeWhisper issues on macOS.
docs.mac.troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
docs.mac.troubleshooting.subtitle: Common issues and how to fix them.
docs.mac.troubleshooting.textInsert.titl: Transcription works but text is not inserted
docs.mac.troubleshooting.textInsert.desc: If you see streaming text in the notch indicator but nothing appears in your target app, the issue is almost always a missing or stale
permission. TypeWhisper needs two separate permissions: Microphone (for recording) and Accessibility (for inserting text). Many users only grant Microphone and miss the second one.
Another sign of this issue is that your
- history entries are only saved after text insertion succeeds.
docs.mac.troubleshooting.textInsert.fix2: If TypeWhisper is listed, remove it (click the minus button)
docs.mac.troubleshooting.textInsert.fix3: Restart TypeWhisper - it will re-prompt for permission
docs.mac.troubleshooting.textInsert.tccD: If that doesn't work, the TCC database entry may be stale. Reset it via Terminal:
docs.mac.troubleshooting.textInsert.tccA: Then restart TypeWhisper and grant Accessibility permission when prompted.
docs.mac.troubleshooting.microphone.desc: If TypeWhisper can't start recording, check
and make sure TypeWhisper is listed and enabled.

On macOS 26 (Tahoe) and later, the Microphone permission dialog only appears once. If you denied it the first time, you need to enable it manually in System Settings. If toggling doesn't help, reset it:
docs.mac.troubleshooting.reinstall.title: Permissions broken after reinstall
docs.mac.troubleshooting.reinstall.desc1: macOS ties permissions to the app's code signature. After reinstalling or updating TypeWhisper, old permission entries can become stale - the toggle appears enabled but the permission doesn't actually work.
docs.mac.troubleshooting.reinstall.desc2: Fix: Remove TypeWhisper from both the Accessibility and Microphone lists in System Settings, restart the app, and re-grant both permissions.
docs.mac.troubleshooting.setupWizard.des: The setup wizard appears automatically when Microphone permission is not granted. Once you grant both Microphone and Accessibility permissions and complete the wizard, it won't appear again.
Live Transcript window stays on screen

If the floating transcript window can be moved between screens, it is probably the Live Transcript plugin window rather than the built-in dictation indicator. The plugin has its own panel and settings.
To stop it appearing automatically, disable Auto-open on recording
To hide or show it manually, assign a Toggle Shortcut
docs.mac.troubleshooting.noAudio.title: No audio input detected
docs.mac.troubleshooting.noAudio.desc1a: If TypeWhisper shows "No audio input available", make sure your microphone is connected and selected. Go to
docs.mac.troubleshooting.noAudio.desc1b: and pick the correct Input Device under Microphone. If using an external microphone, check that it's recognized in System Settings > Sound > Input.
docs.mac.api.meta.title: HTTP API and CLI automation - macOS - TypeWhisper
docs.mac.api.meta.description: Complete TypeWhisper macOS HTTP API reference, including authentication, transcription, settings backup, dictation, Recorder, Dictionary, and CLI examples.
docs.mac.api.title: HTTP API and CLI automation
docs.mac.api.intro1: TypeWhisper includes a versioned local HTTP API for scripts and external tools. The documented
docs.mac.api.intro2: surface covers transcription, app data, settings backups, dictation, Recorder, and workflow-driven automation.
docs.mac.api.noteText: The server is disabled by default and binds only to 127.0.0.1. Do not proxy or expose it to a public network.
docs.mac.api.setup.title: Setup and authentication
docs.mac.api.setup.description: Enable API Server in Settings > Advanced. The default port is 8978; TypeWhisper writes the active port and a generated token to ~/Library/Application Support/TypeWhisper/api-discovery.json while the server is running.
docs.mac.api.auth.description: Require API Token is off by default for compatibility with existing local integrations. When enabled, send the discovery token as a Bearer token on every endpoint except GET /v1/status.
docs.mac.api.auth.statusPublic: GET /v1/status remains public for readiness checks. Clients may alternatively send the same token in the
docs.mac.api.auth.discovery: The discovery file is created with owner-only permissions (0600) and removed when the server stops. The TypeWhisper CLI discovers both its port and token automatically; --port, --api-token, and TYPEWHISPER_API_TOKEN provide explicit overrides.
docs.mac.api.overview.title: Endpoint reference
docs.mac.api.overview.description: The table below reflects all 26 routes registered by the current macOS implementation, including the two legacy /v1/profiles aliases and the settings backup routes.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.status: Report readiness, selected engine/model, API version, and capability flags.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.models: List every model exposed by loaded transcription engines and its current state.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.transcribe: Transcribe multipart or raw audio, with optional language, engine, model, translation, prompt, and correction controls.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.transcribeLocalFil: Transcribe an absolute file path already accessible to the running Mac app; used by the CLI to avoid uploading local files.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.historyDelete: Delete one history entry by UUID.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.termsList: List enabled recognition terms and optional CTC similarity thresholds.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.correctionsPut: Add or update one Dictionary Correction.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.correctionsDelete: Delete one Dictionary Correction by its original text.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.settingsExport: Export the complete Settings Backup JSON document.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.settingsImport: Import a Settings Backup document and return a machine-readable merge/skip summary.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.rulesToggle: Toggle one workflow-backed rule by UUID.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.dictationStart: Start system-wide dictation, optionally forcing an enabled workflow.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.dictationStop: Stop the active API dictation session.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.dictationStatus: Report the live dictation state, model, and active workflow.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.dictationTranscrip: Poll a dictation session for completion, transcription, or failure.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.recorderStart: Start Recorder with optional microphone and system-audio overrides.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.recorderStop: Stop and begin finalizing the active API Recorder session.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.recorderStatus: Report whether Recorder is currently recording.
docs.mac.api.endpoint.recorderSession: Poll a Recorder session for status, text, output file, or failure.
docs.mac.api.checkStatus.title: Check status
docs.mac.api.checkStatus.description: status is ready when the selected model can transcribe and no_model otherwise. Capability fields describe the currently selected engine; nullable engine and model values are omitted when none is selected.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.title: Transcribe audio
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.language: An exact language code such as en or de. Omit it for automatic detection; do not combine it with language_hint.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.languageH: A repeatable, ordered shortlist for restricted automatic detection. Hint-aware engines receive the full list; other engines use the first hint.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.task: transcribe (default) or translate. The translate task translates into English and requires WhisperKit.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.targetLan: A target language code for a separate Apple Translate step. This requires macOS 15 or later.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.responseF: json (default) or verbose_json. Verbose output adds timestamped segments and optional speaker metadata when the engine provides it.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.prompt: A request-specific transcription prompt. TypeWhisper combines it with enabled Dictionary terms.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.engineMod: Per-request engine/model overrides. A model alone is inferred only when exactly one engine offers that ID.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.normalize: A Boolean override for spoken-number normalization.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.applyCorr: A Boolean that defaults to true. Set it to false to return raw engine output without post-transcription Dictionary Corrections.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.params.awaitDown: Wait for an unconfigured local engine to restore or download its model instead of returning 409 immediately.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.uploadLimit.desc: Multipart and raw-body uploads to /v1/transcribe are limited to 256 MiB. Larger requests return 413 Payload Too Large. The macOS CLI uses the local-file route for file paths, while stdin remains subject to this limit.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.rawBody: Raw-body uploads use the Content-Type to infer the audio format and the corresponding X-Language, X-Language-Hints, X-Task, X-Target-Language, X-Response-Format, X-Prompt, X-Engine, X-Model, X-Normalize-Numbers, and X-Apply-Corrections headers for options.
docs.mac.api.transcribe.localFile: accepts a JSON body with an absolute path and the same snake_case options. It is only useful for files readable by the local TypeWhisper process and is not a remote file API.
docs.mac.api.listModels.title: List models
docs.mac.api.listModels.description: status is ready or not_configured. selected identifies the current GUI selection; downloaded and loaded are included when the engine can report those states.
docs.mac.api.history.title: History
docs.mac.api.history.description: q is optional. limit defaults to 50 and is capped at 200; offset defaults to 0. Results include final and raw text, ISO 8601 timestamp, app context, duration, language, engine, model, and word count.
docs.mac.api.dictionary.title: Dictionary
docs.mac.api.dictionary.description: Recognition terms influence transcription. Dictionary Corrections run after transcription and rewrite matching text unless apply_corrections is false.
docs.mac.api.dictionary.termsNote: For simple terms, send a terms string array. For Parakeet CTC tuning, send term_entries with optional ctc_min_similarity. Set replace to true to replace all existing recognition terms; otherwise entries are merged.
docs.mac.api.settings.title: Settings Backup: API and CLI
docs.mac.api.settings.description: The API uses the same schema as Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore. Export includes all supported categories: workflows, Dictionary entries, snippets, prompt actions, profiles, hotkeys, non-bundled plugins, history, update channel, and preferences.
docs.mac.api.settings.importBehavior: Import applies all categories in the document using the existing merge/skip rules. It does not wipe the destination Mac first: workflows and profiles are appended, duplicates can be skipped, occupied hotkey slots are preserved, unavailable or installed plugins are skipped, and history outside the destination retention window is omitted.
docs.mac.api.settings.cliDescription: Install the CLI in Settings > Advanced > Command Line Tool. export writes the API backup atomically; import accepts relative, absolute, and tilde-expanded paths. Add --json for a machine-readable export receipt or import summary.
docs.mac.api.settings.dotfilesNote: A backup can contain transcription history, prompts, app/website rules, and other personal configuration. Review it before committing it to a dotfiles repository. The implementation adds explicit import/export commands; it does not automatically load $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/typewhisper/config.toml.
docs.mac.api.rules.title: Workflow-backed rules
docs.mac.api.rules.description: Each entry includes its UUID, enabled state, priority, app bundle identifiers, URL patterns, language mode and hints, and optional translation target. Use a rule UUID as workflow_id when starting dictation with a forced workflow.
docs.mac.api.rules.legacyAlias: Legacy compatibility: /v1/profiles and /v1/profiles/toggle remain available as exact aliases for older integrations.
docs.mac.api.dictation.title: Dictation control
docs.mac.api.dictation.description: These routes use TypeWhisper's system-wide dictation pipeline and insertion behavior. Start returns a session UUID; stop returns the same UUID so a script can poll its result.
docs.mac.api.dictation.workflow: The start body is optional. When workflow_id is supplied, it must name an existing enabled workflow; TypeWhisper returns the selected workflow ID and name in the start response.
docs.mac.api.dictation.polling: Poll /v1/dictation/transcription until status becomes completed or failed. A completed response contains both final and raw text plus timestamp, app context, duration, language, engine, model, and word count.
docs.mac.api.recorder.title: Recorder control
docs.mac.api.recorder.description: Recorder creates a saved recording and can capture microphone, system audio, or both. It follows the same mixing, finalization, and optional transcription path as the Recorder UI without pasting text into another app.
docs.mac.api.recorder.parameters: mic and system_audio accept true, false, 1, or 0. Omitted values inherit the current Recorder settings, and at least one resolved source must remain enabled.
docs.mac.api.recorder.states: Sessions move through recording, finalizing, and completed or failed. text is omitted when transcription is disabled or empty; output_file is returned when a recording was finalized, and failed sessions include error.
docs.mac.api.errors.title: Error responses
docs.mac.api.errors.description: Failures use a nested JSON error object with code and message fields. Handle the HTTP status first and use message for detail:
docs.mac.api.errors.400: Missing or invalid body, query parameter, file, audio format, workflow ID, or option value.
docs.mac.api.errors.401: Require API Token is enabled and the request has no valid Bearer or X-TypeWhisper-API-Token value.
docs.mac.api.errors.404: A requested history entry, rule, workflow, dictation session, or Recorder session does not exist.
docs.mac.api.errors.409: The requested recording state conflicts with the current state, or an overridden engine is not configured.
docs.mac.api.errors.413: The request body exceeds the 256 MiB upload limit.
docs.mac.api.errors.501: Target-language translation was requested on a macOS version before 15.
docs.mac.api.errors.500: An internal transcription, Dictionary, settings backup, or session error occurred. Check the app logs or diagnostics export for detail.
docs.mac.cli.meta.title: CLI transcription and settings backup - macOS - TypeWhisper
docs.mac.cli.meta.description: Use the typewhisper command-line tool for shell-friendly transcription plus settings backup export and import.
docs.mac.cli.title: CLI Tool
docs.mac.cli.description: A shell-friendly command-line tool that connects to the local TypeWhisper API server for transcription and portable settings backups.
docs.mac.cli.installation.title: Installation
docs.mac.cli.installation.desc1: Install the CLI from the TypeWhisper app: Settings > Advanced > Command Line Tool > Install Command Line Tool. This places the
docs.mac.cli.installation.warning: The TypeWhisper app must be running with the API server enabled. The CLI automatically discovers the current port and token from api-discovery.json.
docs.mac.cli.commands.title: Commands
docs.mac.cli.commands.status: Check if the API server is running and which model is loaded.
docs.mac.cli.commands.models: List all available models and their status.
docs.mac.cli.commands.transcribe: Transcribe an audio file or piped audio input.
docs.mac.cli.commands.export: Export all supported settings to a TypeWhisper Settings Backup JSON file.
docs.mac.cli.commands.import: Import every category in a TypeWhisper Settings Backup file and print a merge/skip summary.
docs.mac.cli.fileSize.title: Large files
docs.mac.cli.fileSize.localFiles: When you pass a local file path, the CLI hands the path to the running TypeWhisper app instead of uploading the file bytes. This avoids the HTTP upload body limit for large recordings.
docs.mac.cli.fileSize.stdin: Piped stdin still uses the /v1/transcribe upload endpoint and is limited to 256 MiB. Larger stdin uploads return 413 Payload Too Large.
docs.mac.cli.settings.title: Settings backup and dotfiles
docs.mac.cli.settings.description: export and import use the same JSON schema as Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore. Relative paths resolve from the current directory, ~ is expanded, and exports are written atomically. Add --json for a machine-readable export receipt or import result.
docs.mac.cli.settings.behavior: Import merges into the destination Mac instead of clearing it first. Workflows and profiles are appended, duplicates and unavailable plugins can be skipped, occupied hotkey slots are preserved, and old history can be excluded by the destination retention policy.
docs.mac.cli.settings.warning: Backups can contain transcription history, prompts, app/website rules, and other personal configuration. Review a backup before committing it to a dotfiles repository. The CLI does not automatically read $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/typewhisper/config.toml.
docs.mac.cli.options.title: Options
docs.mac.cli.options.port: Override the automatically discovered API server port
docs.mac.cli.options.apiToken: Override the discovered Bearer token; TYPEWHISPER_API_TOKEN provides the same override
docs.mac.cli.options.dev: Connect to the TypeWhisper-Dev discovery file instead of the release app
docs.mac.cli.options.helpVersion: Show command help or the installed CLI version
docs.mac.cli.options.languageHint: Repeatable ordered language shortlist; cannot be combined with --language
docs.mac.cli.options.task: transcribe (default) or translate speech to English with WhisperKit
docs.mac.cli.options.translateTo: Run an Apple Translate step for the target language (e.g., de, fr; macOS 15+)
docs.mac.cli.options.engine: Override the transcription engine for this request
docs.mac.cli.options.model: Override the transcription model for this request
docs.mac.cli.options.awaitDownload: Wait for a local engine to restore or download its model instead of returning 409
docs.mac.cli.options.noCorrections: Return raw engine output without post-transcription Dictionary Corrections
